stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Eight states sue OpenAI, saying ChatGPT isn’t safe for kids
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Eight US states have filed lawsuits against OpenAI regarding the safety of ChatGPT.
The lawsuits allege that OpenAI prioritized profits over child safety and misled consumers.
The legal action involves states including Iowa, Kansas, and Arizona.

stories.title: The AI race is back on
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: The AI competitive landscape is intensifying, with Anthropic and OpenAI currently leading the field.
Google and Meta are noted as lagging behind the current leaders in the AI race.
The narrative suggests a significant, ongoing industry shift driven by the rapid advancement of powerful AI models.

stories.title: Researchers use AI to design proteins that cut up other proteins
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: AI is being utilized to engineer novel proteins.
These designed proteins possess the capability to break down highly stable molecular bonds.
The research represents a significant advancement in synthetic biology and protein design.

stories.title: Recording device hidden in toilet paper found in top-secret OpenAI meeting room
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A security breach occurred at OpenAI involving a hidden recording device found in a top-secret meeting room.
An OpenAI engineer is facing serious legal consequences, including a potential 5-year sentence and a $250K fine.
The FBI has implicated foreign spy charges in connection with the incident, highlighting severe security risks in AI development.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its function as a large language model (LLM).
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the current LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The associated tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under text-generation and utilizes transformers and safetensors.
The mention of Llama-3 indicates relevance to the current state of large language models (LLMs).

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model designed specifically for autonomous agents.
The model excels at persistent tasks, including context gathering, tool calling, and multi-step workflows on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round involved prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is serving a substantial developer base of 8.9 million users, indicating strong adoption in the open-source AI space.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: Now that Character.AI is going bankrupt, what happens to all of its users’ data?
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: Character.AI is reportedly filing for bankruptcy, raising immediate concerns about user data.
New York Attorney General Letitia James is leading a multi-state investigation into the company's data practices.
Forty bipartisan Attorneys General have filed notices of interest to address regulatory issues concerning the bankruptcy proceeding.

stories.title: YouTube sticks new labels on AI-generated songs
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: YouTube is implementing new labeling for music tracks that are AI-generated or significantly altered.
This mirrors YouTube's existing policy for labeling AI-generated video content.
The labeling is targeted at specific AI usage in music, not all AI tool applications.

stories.title: Your Transformer Is Secretly Elastic
stories.author: Cees G. M. Snoek
bullet_points: Addresses the rigidity of current transformer models, which are limited to fixed sizes (S, B, L).
Introduces a novel, retraining-free method to make pre-trained transformers 'elastic'.
Allows a single model to dynamically adapt its computational requirements across a continuum of hardware and workloads.

stories.title: Your Transformer Is Secretly Elastic
stories.author: Cees G. M. Snoek
bullet_points: Addresses the rigidity of current transformer models, which are limited to fixed sizes (S, B, L).
Introduces a novel, retraining-free method to make pre-trained transformers 'elastic'.
Allows a single model to dynamically adapt its computational requirements across a continuum of hardware and workload demands.

stories.title: GitLab warns of max severity code execution vulnerability
stories.author: bleepingcomputer.com via janus
bullet_points: GitLab has issued a warning regarding a critical vulnerability.
The vulnerability is classified as having 'max severity' and involves code execution.
This is significant security news impacting users of the GitLab platform.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the safe execution of AI agents.
The integration allows these agents to run within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for secure, cloud-based deployment of local AI models.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, typed decision-making based on text input.
The feature allows for low-latency, cost-free answering of yes/no questions, choices, and scoring with probabilities.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to leverage open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: McKinsey is making job applicants spar with a fake AI client
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: McKinsey is integrating an AI simulation into its entry-level interview process.
The AI is designed to mimic 80% of the real-world client scenarios consultants face.
This signals a growing trend of using generative AI for practical, high-stakes hiring simulations.

stories.title: Microsoft and Japan took down a cybercrime network behind over a billion scam messages
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Microsoft collaborated with Japan's National Police Agency to dismantle a large-scale cybercrime network.
The network was responsible for distributing over a billion scam and phishing messages globally.
The operation targets common scams, such as fake parking tickets and package delivery notifications.

stories.title: Fridge hack costing millions and sparking fires stemmed from poor security
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A security vulnerability in supermarket refrigeration units led to a major incident.
The hack exploited outdated devices that were improperly exposed to the internet.
The incident resulted in significant costs and caused fires across 700 supermarkets.

stories.title: NATO may redeploy anti-drone defenses as attacks sink more Black Sea shipping
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: NATO is considering redeploying anti-drone defense systems.
The threat stems from suspected Russian drone attacks.
Multiple commercial shipping vessels have been sunk or damaged in the Black Sea region.

stories.title: Things are finally looking up for NASA's first missions to Venus in a generation
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: NASA is making significant progress on its upcoming missions to Venus.
The positive outlook is prompting NASA to increase staffing and accelerate mission timelines.
The news represents a major step forward for planetary exploration in a long period.

stories.title: Georgia man sues Flock, sheriff's office over alleged ALPR-fueled retaliation
stories.author: Cyrus Farivar
bullet_points: A Georgia resident is suing Flock and the local sheriff's office.
The lawsuit alleges that Automated License Plate Readers (ALPR) cameras were used for warrantless tracking and monitoring.
The alleged surveillance followed a prior lawsuit filed by the plaintiff regarding excessive force.

stories.title: Modeling and Understanding Neural Weights of Humanoid Policies with Diffusion
stories.author: Koushil Sreenath
bullet_points: The research focuses on modeling and understanding the neural weights of humanoid control policies.
It addresses a gap in current robot learning by moving beyond conventional training to model weight distributions directly.
The work investigates using diffusion models to generate functional humanoid control networks in weight space.

stories.title: Hierarchical Residual Policy Learning for Real-World Mobile Manipulation with Sparse Human Guidance
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of real-world fine-tuning for complex Mobile Manipulation (MoMa) systems.
Introduces HiRe-MoMa, a framework utilizing a Hierarchical Residual Architecture for stable and sample-efficient learning.
Focuses on overcoming high-dimensional action spaces and module coupling in robotic systems.

stories.title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
stories.author: Jiaxuan You
bullet_points: Addresses the high computational cost of long-horizon rollouts in training language agents.
Proposes a novel method to better utilize intermediate-step supervision, which is often ignored in standard RL.
Attempts to overcome limitations in existing supervision techniques, such as value targets derived from a single terminal scalar reward.

stories.title: Continuum Attention
stories.author: Afshin Khadangi
bullet_points: Introduces Continuum Attention (CA), a novel causal Transformer attention operator.
Replaces discrete key/value lookup with integration over a continuous, piecewise linear memory curve.
Achieves exact normalized attention via closed-form exponential moments, simplifying gradient calculation.

stories.title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
stories.author: Hwee Tou Ng
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of training AI agents to master complex, visually rich video games.
Current methods are limited by reliance on large demonstrations and difficulty in creating scalable training environments.
The paper introduces 'Player-1' to advance general digital control by enabling learning from synthetic experience.

stories.title: One Task, Many Interfaces: Simple Cross-Interface Consistency Training Improves LLM Agent Robustness
stories.author: Peng Qi
bullet_points: LLM agents suffer from interface binding, meaning their performance degrades when the input interface is slightly altered from the training setup.
The paper proposes 'Cross-Interface Consistency Training' to improve the robustness of LLM agents against interface variations.
The research addresses the limitation of current methods, which only broaden dependence on the training interface distribution rather than eliminating it.

stories.title: Beyond LLM Judge: Mechanical Verification for Agentic Autoformalization
stories.author: Michael R. Douglas
bullet_points: Introduces a novel verification method for Lean formalizations that moves beyond reliance on LLM judgment.
The method integrates LLM-based semantic review with rigorous mechanical numerical and vacuity checks for enhanced accuracy.
The technique is applied within an Extract-Verify-Proof pipeline to construct the Formalized Library of Mathematical Functions (FLMF).

stories.title: Recovering Reliable Supervision via Critique-Guided On-Policy Distillation
stories.author: Taylor W. Killian
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in On-Policy Distillation (OPD) where teacher models fail to provide reliable supervision on incorrect student rollouts.
The core problem identified is the 'recoverability of the teacher,' which breaks down when the student makes errors.
The proposed solution, CriticOPD, uses a critic mechanism to allow the teacher to critique incorrect rollouts, thereby restoring reliable supervision.

stories.title: Modeling and Understanding Neural Weights of Humanoid Policies with Diffusion
stories.author: Koushil Sreenath
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap in humanoid control by focusing on modeling the distribution of learned neural network weights.
It proposes using diffusion models to generate functional humanoid control networks directly in weight space.
This work aims to move beyond conventional training procedures to better understand and generate high-performing robotic policies.

stories.title: Hierarchical Residual Policy Learning for Real-World Mobile Manipulation with Sparse Human Guidance
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of real-world fine-tuning in Mobile Manipulation (MoMa) due to high-dimensional action spaces.
Introduces HiRe-MoMa, a framework utilizing a Hierarchical Residual Architecture for stable and sample-efficient fine-tuning.
Focuses on improving complex MoMa systems using sparse human guidance.

stories.title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
stories.author: Jiaxuan You
bullet_points: The research addresses the high computational cost of long-horizon rollouts in training language agents.
It critiques existing reinforcement learning methods that waste intermediate step supervision by relying only on a terminal scalar reward.
The proposed method aims to improve supervision by co-evolving acting and forecasting, overcoming limitations in traditional value or observation targets.

stories.title: Continuum Attention
stories.author: Afshin Khadangi
bullet_points: Introduces Continuum Attention (CA), a novel causal Transformer attention operator.
Replaces discrete key/value lookup with integration over a continuous, piecewise linear memory curve.
Achieves exact normalized attention via closed-form exponential moments, enabling analytical gradient calculation.

stories.title: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training
stories.author: Xu Han
bullet_points: Addresses the memory and computational bottleneck caused by large Key-Value (KV) caches in long-context LLMs.
Introduces 'Latent Compaction,' a method that learns a compact, document-specific cache via test-time training.
Uses initialization techniques (reconstruction importance, teacher attention, key-space diversity) to ensure information preservation during compression.

stories.title: One Task, Many Interfaces: Simple Cross-Interface Consistency Training Improves LLM Agent Robustness
stories.author: Peng Qi
bullet_points: LLM agents exhibit interface dependence, meaning their performance degrades when the input interface is slightly changed (e.g., renaming an action).
The paper proposes 'Cross-Interface Consistency Training' to improve the robustness of LLM agents against these interface variations.
The research addresses the limitation of current methods where interface randomization only broadens dependence rather than eliminating it for out-of-distribution perturbations.

stories.title: Recovering Reliable Supervision via Critique-Guided On-Policy Distillation
stories.author: Taylor W. Killian
bullet_points: Addresses a critical failure in On-Policy Distillation (OPD) where teacher models fail to recover from student errors.
Introduces 'CriticOPD,' a novel method that uses a critic to guide the teacher's critique of incorrect student rollouts.
Focuses on improving the reliability and robustness of knowledge transfer in large language model training.

stories.title: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training
stories.author: Xu Han
bullet_points: Addresses the memory and computational bottleneck caused by large Key-Value (KV) caches in long-context LLMs.
Proposes 'Latent Compaction,' a method that learns a compact, document-specific cache via test-time training.
Utilizes initialization techniques based on reconstruction importance, teacher attention, and key-space diversity.

stories.title: One Task, Many Interfaces: Simple Cross-Interface Consistency Training Improves LLM Agent Robustness
stories.author: Peng Qi
bullet_points: LLM agents exhibit interface dependence, meaning their performance degrades when the input interface is slightly modified from the training setup.
The paper proposes 'Cross-Interface Consistency Training' to improve LLM agent robustness against interface variations.
The core problem addressed is that current methods only broaden dependence across a distribution of training interfaces, failing against unseen perturbations.

stories.title: Manacá-1B-Instruct-2: Reproducible Safety Alignment for a Native Brazilian-Portuguese LLM. Negative DPO Results, a Controlled Composition Scan, and a Silent Failure Mode of the LLM Judge
stories.author: Fabio André Machado Porto
bullet_points: Introduces Manacá-1B-Instruct-2, a new, safety-aligned LLM specifically trained for Brazilian Portuguese (PT-BR).
Highlights the importance of documenting failures in alignment, presenting three negative Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) attempts.
Examines the limitations of LLM judges, noting a 'silent failure mode' in the evaluation process.

stories.title: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
stories.author: Matei Zaharia
bullet_points: LLM agents are demonstrating capability in automated research and idea discovery through iterative refinement.
Scaling automated research via longer iteration, parallel agents, or agent communication eventually leads to performance plateaus.
The research suggests that 'forgetting' is a necessary mechanism to overcome the limitations of accumulating excessive history in LLM agents.

stories.title: PerSo: Investigating Facets of LLMs' Social Intelligence in Real-World Persuasion Scenarios
stories.author: Yadollah Yaghoobzadeh
bullet_points: The research investigates the 'social intelligence' of Large Language Models (LLMs) using real-world persuasion scenarios.
Social intelligence is defined by two facets: cognitive intelligence (inferring mental states) and behavioral intelligence (selecting appropriate social actions).
Persuasion serves as a natural and complex testbed to evaluate both the cognitive and behavioral aspects of LLM social capabilities.

stories.title: PrismaCoder: Pushing the Boundaries of Open Multimodal Code Intelligence through Decomposed Rubric Synthesis
stories.author: Jiahui Gao
bullet_points: The research introduces 'PrismaCoder,' focusing on open multimodal code intelligence.
The field connects symbolic code with visual outputs (charts, webpages, animations).
The work aims to advance open-source capabilities against proprietary models that currently lead in this area.

stories.title: VASPO: Self-Distillation with Privileged Value Estimation
stories.author: Jun Du
bullet_points: Introduces VASPO, a new method for self-distillation in reasoning models.
Addresses a limitation in current self-distillation techniques where supervision reflects local token preferences, not expected return.
Proposes a more effective integration of privileged teacher signals within the PPO framework, contrasting with existing GRPO combinations.

stories.title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models
stories.author: Chuan-Wei Kuo
bullet_points: ReaDy introduces a novel speculative decoding method for LLMs.
It leverages Hybrid Linear Attention (HLA) models, which maintain compact recurrent states for context.
This approach addresses limitations in feature-based drafters by providing complementary historical context for efficient token drafting.

stories.title: Lost in Translation: Why Lower Bias Scores Don't Mean Fairer Models
stories.author: Harsh Kumar
bullet_points: The paper challenges the standard practice of using simple average stereotype score differences between English and other languages to measure model fairness.
Researchers investigated the impact of linguistic noise by rephrasing English test items and testing language-specific shifts across ten open models in eight languages.
The study aims to determine how much of the observed 'bias difference' in multilingual models is attributable to linguistic noise rather than genuine bias.

stories.title: AdaRSI: On-Demand Recursive Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
stories.author: Daling Wang
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models: failure during long-horizon, unseen tasks.
Proposes AdaRSI, a method for On-Demand Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) in embodied agents.
Distinguishes between failures caused by incorrect executor invocation versus inherent executor capability limitations.

stories.title: Wanted to download an ISO, ended up writing a kernel exploit
stories.author: 0xdeafbeef
bullet_points: A user discovered a kernel exploit while attempting to download an ISO.
The vulnerability affects at least 13 in-tree drivers, exhibiting silent data corruption on non-coherent architectures (like ARM).
The author is seeking guidance on proper driver implementation, specifically regarding cache maintenance and the use of the DMA API.
